_meta.description: Document-rules config for plaint_specific_performance — suit for specific performance of contract under S.10-14 Specific Relief Act, 1963 (post-2018 amendment)
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Readiness and willingness pleading is non-negotiable. Post-2018 SRA amendment treats SP as general rule.

title: Plaint — Suit for Specific Performance of Contract

Time stipulated for performance (and whether 'time is of essence')
Whether time was of the essence
Plaintiff's part-performance / acts done (paid earnest, ready to pay balance, possession taken)
Plaintiff's continuous readiness and willingness — specific pleadings of financial capacity and steps taken

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, aged about {plaintiff_age} years, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above plaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a plaint for specific performance of contract under Sections 10-14 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

POST-2018 AMENDMENT (Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018, w.e.f. 01.10.2018) FUNDAMENTAL CHANGE: Specific performance is now the GENERAL RULE, not the exception. Pre-amendment S.10 conferred discretion ('may be enforced') — post-amendment it MUST be enforced subject to exceptions in S.11(2), S.14, S.16.
S.10 (post-amendment): Specific performance shall be enforced subject to provisions of S.11(2), 14, and 16.
S.11: Cases in which SP enforceable when act required to be performed in performance of trust.

S.14 (post-amendment) — Contracts NOT specifically enforceable (exhaustive list): (a) where party suffered substituted performance under S.20; (b) involving continuous duty which court cannot supervise; (c) dependent on personal qualifications of parties; (d) determinable in nature.

S.16 — Personal bars to relief: (a) party who would not be entitled to recover compensation; (b) party who becomes incapable of performing; (c) party who fails to aver and prove that he has performed or has always been ready and willing to perform essential terms of the contract.

S.16(c) READINESS AND WILLINGNESS — MANDATORY PLEADING. Plaintiff MUST plead continuous readiness and willingness. Pleading of mere 'ready and willing' insufficient — must plead specific acts: earnest paid, balance kept ready, financial capacity, performance of conditions precedent.
Cite: Syed Dastagir v. T.R. Gopalakrishna Setty (1999) 6 SCC 337 — readiness implies financial capacity; willingness implies conduct.
Cite: J.P. Builders v. A. Ramadas Rao (2011) 1 SCC 429 — readiness and willingness must be continuous throughout.
Cite: Beemaiah v. Govindappa (2013) 11 SCC 754 — pleadings of readiness and willingness essential; absence fatal.
Cite: Kamal Kumar v. Premlata Joshi (2019) 3 SCC 704 — explanation to S.16(c) post-2018 — actual tender of money not necessary; willingness to pay must be averred.
Para 1-2: Parties description.
Para 3: Existence and terms of contract — date, mode (written/oral), consideration, time for performance.
Para 4: Subject-matter description — for immovable property, full schedule with boundaries.
Para 5: Plaintiff's part-performance — earnest paid, possession taken (if any), other acts.
Para 6: SPECIFIC pleading of plaintiff's readiness and willingness throughout — show source of funds, bank balance, sale of other assets if any. Plead willingness to perform balance obligations.
Para 7: Defendant's breach / refusal — specific acts and dates. Where defendant alleges time of essence and seeks to terminate, address that.
Para 8: Legal notice calling upon defendant to perform — date and reply.

Para 9: Time of essence analysis — generally in immovable property transactions, time is NOT of the essence (Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani; Saradamani Kandappan v. Rajalakshmi (2011) 12 SCC 18 — but plaintiff must still act with reasonable diligence).
Para 10: Confirm contract not within S.14 exceptions.
Para 11: Alternative relief under S.21 SRA — claim damages in alternative.
Para 12: Cause of action — date of fixed performance or, if no date fixed, date plaintiff had notice that defendant refused.
Para 13: Limitation — Article 54 Limitation Act — 3 years from date fixed for performance, or, if none fixed, from when plaintiff had notice of refusal.
Para 14: Jurisdiction — S.16 CPC for immovable property suits.
Para 15: Court fee — ad valorem on consideration (state Court Fees Act).
If commercial dispute u/s 2(1)(c) CCA 2015 and value >=Rs.3 lakh: Commercial Court track + pre-institution mediation u/s 12A (Patil Automation).
Note S.19A SRA — substituted performance of contracts (post-2018).
Tone: precise. Avoid argumentative.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

relevantActs.act: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (as amended by Act 18 of 2018)

sections.description: Cases in which specific performance enforceable — post-2018 mandatory subject to exceptions
Rights of purchaser against person with no title or imperfect title
Relief against parties and persons claiming under them
Power to award compensation in certain cases
Power to grant relief for possession, partition, refund of earnest
Application of preceding sections to awards
Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract where time is essential
Sale defined; contract for sale does not create interest
Execution of decree for execution of document
Suit for SP — 3 years from date fixed or notice of refusal
Construction of immovable property within commercial dispute definition
SP suits — ad valorem on consideration

filing_checklist: Affidavit in support of plaint (Order VI R.15(4))
Statement of truth (if Commercial Court — Order VI R.15A)
Court fee — ad valorem on consideration (state Schedule)
Receipts / bank statements showing earnest payment
Title chain of defendant (sale deed, mutation, parent deeds)
Legal notice calling for performance + reply
Plaintiff's bank statement / FD / sale-proceed evidence showing financial readiness
Stamp papers ready for sale deed execution (or undertaking to procure)
Pre-institution mediation non-starter certificate (if commercial and applicable)
Application under Order 39 R.1-2 if status quo / restraint on alienation sought
Application u/s 52 TPA — lis pendens registration
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: plaintiff_name and defendant_name must not be empty
readiness_willingness must not be empty — and must include specific acts (S.16(c) mandate)
alternative_relief_damages must be true (always plead alternative damages)
If commercial_dispute=true and no urgent interim relief, pre_institution_mediation must be true
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Beemaiah v. Govindappa (2013) 11 SCC 754 — Readiness and willingness pleading mandatory
Syed Dastagir v. T.R. Gopalakrishna Setty (1999) 6 SCC 337 — Readiness = financial capacity; willingness = conduct
J.P. Builders v. A. Ramadas Rao (2011) 1 SCC 429 — Continuous readiness and willingness
Kamal Kumar v. Premlata Joshi (2019) 3 SCC 704 — Post-2018 amendment; actual tender unnecessary
Saradamani Kandappan v. Rajalakshmi (2011) 12 SCC 18 — Time of essence in immovable property — modern approach
Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani (1993) 1 SCC 519 — Time generally not of essence in property contracts
Katta Sujatha Reddy v. Siddamsetty Infra Projects (2022) — Post-2018 amendment applies prospectively to contracts entered after 01.10.2018
K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan (1997) 3 SCC 1 — Plaintiff must explain delay even where time not of essence
